name: Breakeven Units
description: Calculate the sales volume required to cover fixed costs.
formula: Breakeven units = Fixed costs / (Price − Variable cost per unit)
business_contexts: a startup determining how many units it must sell to cover its fixed overhead
a restaurant determining how many covers it needs to break even each month
a manufacturer determining the volume needed to cover plant fixed costs
a software company determining how many seats it needs to cover fixed hosting and support costs
an event organizer determining how many tickets must sell to break even
question_patterns: Given the fixed costs, price, and variable cost per unit below, how many units must be sold to break even?
Calculate the breakeven volume from the figures given.
How many units are needed to cover the fixed costs shown, at the price and cost given?
Calculate the sales volume required to break even, given the figures below.
Using the fixed costs and per-unit economics given, what is the breakeven unit volume?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate contribution margin per unit = price_per_unit − variable_cost_per_unit
Step 2: Calculate breakeven units = fixed_costs / contribution margin per unit
key_insight: Breakeven volume is fixed costs divided by contribution margin, never by price — the variable cost per unit has to come out first.
common_mistakes: Dividing fixed costs by price instead of by contribution margin
Forgetting to subtract variable cost per unit before dividing
framework_soundbite: Fixed costs over contribution margin — the denominator is what's left after variable cost, not the sticker price.
